Day in Our Data · Saturday, October 3, 2026, 11 a.m. to 3 p.m.

From idea to demo: the workflow

AI makes writing code fast. What still takes judgment is deciding what to build, checking that it is right, and keeping track of what you learned. This is a loop you can run several times in one afternoon.

On this page

  1. The loop
  2. The loop on the day
  3. A typical prototype architecture
  4. Who does what
  5. Compound Engineering in one page

The loop

Five stages. Humans own the decisions; Claude does most of the typing. The last stage feeds the first: each loop starts smarter than the one before. The commands in each box come from the Compound Engineering plugin.

The loop on the day

The event runs 11 to 3. A realistic plan is one full loop before lunch and a second, smaller loop after.

A typical prototype architecture

Most Day in Our Data projects share one shape. Name each box when you ask Claude to plan, and it will build in that order.

Who does what

Human and AI responsibilities at each stage
StageThe team decidesClaude doesPrompt to try
BrainstormWhich question matters to residentsAsks clarifying questions, suggests anglesInterview us about starter project 6 until you can write a one-paragraph goal.
PlanWhat is in and out of scopeDrafts steps, flags risks and unknownsPlan this in 5 steps. Mark the must-have demo and what to cut first.
ArchitectureMap or chart? Page or notebook?Proposes files, libraries, and data flowPropose the simplest architecture. No databases unless we need one.
BuildWhen a step is good enoughWrites and runs code, fixes its own errorsDo step 1 only, then tell me how to open the result.
QAWhether the numbers are believableWrites tests, reviews code, checks accessibilityWrite tests that compare your totals to the raw CSV, then run them.
CompoundWhat to remember next timeWrites notes into CLAUDE.md or docs/Add what we learned today to CLAUDE.md.

Compound Engineering in one page

Main commands from the Compound Engineering plugin
Type thisWhat it does
/ce-ideateNot sure what to build? Explore options first.
/ce-brainstormQuestion-and-answer session that ends in a written requirements plan.
/ce-planTurn requirements into a step-by-step implementation plan.
/ce-workCarry out the plan, writing and running the code.
/ce-simplify-codeTidy fresh code for clarity and reuse.
/ce-code-reviewSeveral reviewer agents check the work against the plan.
/ce-compoundRecord the lessons in docs/solutions/ so the next loop starts smarter.
/ce-debugStart from a bug report instead of a feature.
/lfgRun the whole pipeline hands-off. Fun to watch; review everything it produces.

No plugin? Same loop, plain English

Everything above works without installing anything. Use plan mode (Shift+Tab) for brainstorm, plan, and architecture; say go to build; ask for tests and a review for QA; ask Claude to update CLAUDE.md to compound.

Found a mistake? These pages are built from guides/pages/workflow.toml in the showcase repository. Pull requests welcome.
